facts.fact_text: At the time of the applicant's arrest on 17 November 2012, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that any breach of the rules, set forth under the legislation, on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen Azerbaijani manats.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 17 November 2012, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with a lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five Azerbaijani manats or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by administrative detention for a term of up to fifteen days.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences concerning breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced for the first time a punishment in the form of administrative detention of up to fifteen days for breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
Law no. 457-IVQD of 2 November 2012 increased the fine set out in Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences to AZN 200.

In the second case (26 January 2013), the applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences, which concerns participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law.
The two police officers questioned in the second case testified that they had arrested the applicant because he had staged an unauthorised demonstration.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe raised concern about recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which increased penalties for the organisers of, and participants in, 'unauthorised' gatherings.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated that the square where the organisers proposed to hold the assembly of 17 November 2012 was a designated public leisure area.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated that the assembly of 17 November 2012 was impractical.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks stated that the sanctions which can now be imposed, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations in Azerbaijan.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks stated that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks urged the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
According to the applicant, he was never served with copies of the administrative-offence reports from his case files.
According to the applicant, he was never served with other documents from his case files.
According to the applicant, in neither the first case (17 November 2012) nor the second case (26 January 2013) was he given access to a lawyer after his arrest or while in police custody.

According to the applicant, members of the public were not allowed to attend the court hearings in either case, even though the court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearings to the public.
According to the applicant, in neither the first case (17 November 2012) nor the second case (26 January 2013) was he given an opportunity to hire a lawyer of his own choice.
In his appeals before the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicant complained that the hearings before the respective first-instance courts had not been fair.
In the first case (17 November 2012), the applicant was assisted before the Baku Court of Appeal by a lawyer of his own choice.
In the second case (26 January 2013), the applicant was not represented by a lawyer before the Baku Court of Appeal.
The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 was authored by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks stated that the Commissioner is deeply concerned by the recent amendments to the Law on Freedom of Assembly, the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which further erode the right to freedom of assembly.
